subject: 2021-2022 Back-to-School Reopening and Safety Plans
overview: District administrators presented updates on curriculum, special education, and facility operations ahead of the 2021-2022 school year. The forum focused heavily on COVID-19 mitigation strategies, including a new agreement with the teachers' union regarding vaccination documentation and testing.

items.title: Opening Remarks and Team Introductions
items.summary: Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent and the district leadership team introduced the session as an opportunity to address community questions regarding the upcoming school year.

items.title: Special Education and Disability Services Updates
items.summary: Director Joan Bowen detailed new administrative hires, year-long professional development for IEP writing, and the implementation of a disability awareness curriculum across grade levels.

items.title: Elementary Education and Social-Emotional Learning
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Suzanne Galusi described the 'Responsive Classroom' initiative for building school culture and introduced 'Nexus,' a new special class focused on executive functioning and social skills.

items.title: Secondary Education and Vocational Grant
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent Peter Cushing announced updated science textbooks, new assistant principals, and a $400,000 grant to support the vocational curriculum and student voice initiatives.

items.title: COVID-19 Health and Safety Protocols
items.summary: Assistant Superintendent David Murphy outlined a tentative agreement with the teachers' union requiring weekly testing and proof of vaccination, alongside a continued partnership with Tufts University for student pooled testing.

items.title: Public Q&A: Quarantine, Masks, and Facilities
items.summary: Superintendent Edouard-Vincent confirmed that remote learning is not an option this year, while administrators detailed indoor and outdoor lunch protocols, air filtration investments, and the requirement for new testing consent forms.
